title: Mom's Chow-Chow
totalTime: About 2 days, including overnight salting and 24 hours to seal

items.text: 1 medium head cabbage (about 4 cups finely chopped)
½ cup salt, for the overnight salting

steps.text: Pulse the cabbage, green tomatoes, onions, and red and yellow peppers in a blender, in batches.
steps.donenessCue: Small, even, relish-size pieces, not purée. You want about 4 cups each of cabbage, tomato and onion.

steps.text: Put all the vegetables in a large glass or porcelain container. Sprinkle with ½ cup salt, cover, and refrigerate overnight.
Drain the vegetables in a colander and rinse with water, in small batches if needed. Let them drain thoroughly, then put them in a large stockpot.
Stir together 4 cups sugar, 3 tbsp mustard seed, 2 tbsp celery seed, 1 tbsp turmeric, 4 cups white vinegar and 2 cups water. Pour over the vegetables.
Bring to a boil and boil 5–6 minutes.
Taste, and adjust the spices before canning.
Ladle into hot, sterilized pint jars, leaving ½ inch of space at the top.
Run a clean utensil around the inside of each jar to release air bubbles.
Wipe the jar rims clean. Put on the lids and screw the bands on tightly.
Lower the jars into boiling water in a canning pot and boil 10 minutes.
Lift the jars out and let them stand undisturbed for 24 hours.
steps.donenessCue: Every lid is sealed: pressed in the center, it doesn't flex or pop back.

ifYouFeelLikeIt: Add chopped jalapeños with the vegetables for a spicy version, to taste.
storage: Sealed jars keep in a cool, dark place for up to 2 years. Any jar that didn't seal goes in the fridge and gets used first.
